skeleton:
Boulettes de Poisson — Fish Balls in the Chermoula Pan

Tunisian · Medium · 6

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The boulettes de poisson are the #51's sardine-meatball doctrine run at the white-fish register — the same fish-forced meatballs, the same simmer-in-the-sauce architecture, the bind and the poach unchanged — but built from the market's firm white fish and carried by the #93 chermoula's marinade rather than the sardine's own assertive oil. This record is the technique's second seat; the fish-meatball law is the master's.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

Ingredients

- **The boulette's law, carried from the master: the forcemeat's bind tested before the pot.** The minced fish runs wetter than the sardine's own paste, and the bind's test (the pressed spoonful holding its shape, the weep's absence) is the whole insurance — the white fish's boulettes are the family's most fragile members at the poach, and the chill's 30 minutes before the sauce's entry is the shape's own mercy. - **The bridge:** the #51 master carries the fish-meatball doctrine whole (the bind, the sauce's simmer, the poach's gentleness); the #93 chermoula carries the marinade; the #76/#79 croquette family runs the fried counterpoint — the poached boulette and the fried cake are the fish-economy's two answers.

Boulettes de Poisson — Fish Balls in the Chermoula Pan

Prep: 30 min (plus 30 min chill) · Cook: 40 min · Total: 1 h 40 min · 6

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 700 g firm white fish (hake, whiting, or grouper), finely minced or food-processed to a coarse paste
  • 1 small onion (about 150 g), grated and squeezed near-dry
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 egg (about 50 g)
  • 3 tbsp breadcrumbs or matza meal (about 25 g)
  • ¼ cup chopped parsley and cilantro, mixed (about 20 g)
  • 1 tsp ground cumin, ½ tsp sweet paprika
  • Grated zest of 1 lemon
  • 1 tsp salt
  • For the sauce: 3 tbsp olive oil (about 40 g), 1 onion sliced, 3 garlic cloves, 2 tsp harissa (#91) or 2 tsp tomato paste plus 1 tsp harissa, 700 g tomatoes grated, 1 tsp cumin, 250 ml water
  • The #93 chermoula's half-batch, the boulettes' 30-minute marinade

Instructions

  1. **The marinade (30 minutes).** The minced fish folded through the #93 chermoula's half-batch; the bowl chilled 30 minutes — the chermoula's acid and the oil working the fish's fibers at the cold's pace. Checkpoint — the marinade's law: the chermoula's coat on every strand of the mince, the bowl's chill held — the fish's cold is the forcemeat's own safety and the shape's own firmness at the shaping.
  2. **The forcemeat and the bind's test (10 minutes).** The onion, garlic, egg, breadcrumbs, herbs, cumin, paprika, lemon zest, and salt worked through the marinated fish — the mixture homogeneous, moist, holding. Checkpoint — the master's own test: a pressed spoonful keeps its dome without weeping — the white fish's wetter mince demands the breadcrumb's honest mercy more than the sardine's own paste ever did; the weep's addition is the collapse's own future in the sauce.
  3. **The shaping and the chill's extension.** The mixture rolled to 18–20 balls (about 45 g each) — the palms' gentle round, never the squeeze's density — the tray held chilled while the sauce builds. Checkpoint — the round's law: smooth-faced and holding the palm's release — the cracked or soft ball returns to the bowl for another breadcrumb's mercy, because the sauce's poach forgives nothing at the shape's edge.
  4. **The sauce and the poach (35 minutes).** The oil in the wide pan; the onion softened 6 minutes, the garlic and the harissa-tomato fried to the bloom, the tomatoes and cumin in and simmered 10 minutes to the thickened base, the water stirred in. The boulettes lowered into the barely-simmering sauce — never dropped at the boil — the pot held at the shiver's poach (the 85 °C order), covered, 18–20 minutes, turned once at the halfway's mercy. Checkpoint — eating test: the boulette's yield — tender to the spoon's edge, the chermoula's perfume and the white fish's sweetness run through by the sauce's fire — the sauce itself carrying the marinade's escaped oil, richer for the boulettes' passage. It should taste like the fish-economy's Sunday argument — the market's firm flesh made the family's pot, the chermoula's lemon-garlic law inside every ball.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Boulettes crumbled in the sauceThe bind's weep or the pot's boilThe spoonful's test; the shiver's poach
Interior blandThe marinade's rushThe chermoula's full 30 minutes
Balls dense, mealyThe palms' squeezeThe gentle round — the squeeze's density poaches to the matzoh ball's heaviness

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- Keeps 3 days refrigerated, the boulettes improving in the sauce's marriage — the gentle reheat's law (the shiver, never the boil) carried through the pot's whole life. The variations: the sardine's own return to the master's seat (#51), the shrimp's coastal dial, the Pesach register (the matza meal's bind).
